pick.headline: Raul Alfonsin elected president of Argentina
pick.summary: On October 30, 1983, Raul Alfonsin of the Radical Civic Union won Argentina's presidential election, ending seven years of military rule.
pick.significance: His government prosecuted the junta leaders for the 'dirty war' disappearances.
pick.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of October 31, 1983, opened with Argentina: the UCR victorious, the Peronist spokesman admitting defeat, Alfonsin's victory speech and call for reconciliation, and plans for the transfer of power.

alternates.headline: Madrid Middle East peace conference opens
alternates.summary: On October 30, 1991, the Middle East peace conference opened in Madrid, bringing Israel face to face with Syria, Lebanon and a joint Jordanian-Palestinian delegation.
alternates.significance: The conference, co-sponsored by the US and USSR after the Gulf War, began the direct negotiations that led to the Oslo accords.
alternates.fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of October 30, 1991, carried Israeli coverage of the Madrid conference: Netanyahu insisting talks be held in the region, and YEDI'OT AHARONOT on Shamir's letter to Baker refusing to discuss Jerusalem.
